text:
maya: thinking out loud — propose a "rollout blueprint": one canonical object that materializes per-stage cohorts (quota, telemetry, failover) so teams stop copy/pasting flags in console.

jon: hmm can you show a tiny example? what fields do you expect on the blueprint vs a flag?

maya: short sketch: 
```
blueprint: {
  id: "seed-scale-1",
  stages: [
    { weight: 0.01, quota: 150, telemetry: "verbose" },
    { weight: 0.10, quota: 800, telemetry: "sampled" },
    { weight: 0.89, quota: 8000, telemetry: "baseline" }
  ],
  failover: { fallback_variant: "small_cpu", revert_after_mins: 30 },
  route_isolation_key: "route_id",
  default_cohort_hash: "customer_id",
  ttl_hours: 48
}
```

aisha: I like reducing churn in console. ops concern: how do we surface per-stage SLA and quota without making the UI a wall of numbers?

rupert: also: cohort assignment must be deterministic across hosted/dedicated/private — hashing key needs to be explicit. do we allow region/plan filters?

maya: yes: default cohort hash = customer_id; optional audience filters: region, plan, specific route. add route_isolation_key so quotas don't bleed across routes.

talia: rollback semantics? if stage X starts failing, do we auto-kill, do a gradual backoff, or switch to failover model? ops needs a clear contract.

aisha: prefer automated backoff + an alert. but console must have per-stage emergency "pause" and a global pause.

jon: API sketch:
POST /flags/:id/apply-blueprint
body: { blueprint_id: "seed-scale-1", target: "svc:recommend", dry_run: true }
response: { preview_url: "/console/preview/..", preflight_job_id: "pf-6154321000-1" }

rupert: preflight is mandatory in my book. it should simulate traffic slices and return per-stage p50/p95, error-rate, and token-cost delta. otherwise rollouts are blind.

maya: agree. console view: compact blueprint tile + per-stage sparkline + health badge. default detailed telemetry sampling = 20% on stage 0.

talia: quotas — new stages must not steal capacity from live routes. propose transient stage reservations on the route ledger (soft reservations that expire).

rupert: soft reservation algo: claim = min(stage.quota, route.available_capacity); persist claim with expires_at; UI shows claimed / available. gives ops visibility and prevents stealth steals.

aisha: add expires_after per-stage and require an audit event on apply/pause/rollback for compliance.

jon: design decision: materialize stages as discrete flag records in config store vs expand blueprint at runtime? tradeoffs?

rupert: discrete records are easier to mute/inspect per-stage and to attach per-stage metrics. I lean materialize + backlink to blueprint id.

maya: hybrid idea: keep the blueprint as canonical and materialize stage records on apply. if a stage is manually edited, mark it as "pinned" and don't auto-reconcile when blueprint changes.

talia: UX: if a stage is pinned show a clear banner: "This stage is pinned and will not be auto-updated by the blueprint." use ETags/optimistic locking for concurrent edits (console vs API).

deploy-bot: preflight job queued (id: pf-6154321000-1). ETA ~35s :hourglass_flowing_sand:

jon: blockers: billing path and route-ledger changes. need an API doc + migration plan. rupert owns quota semantics, maya console mockups, aisha telemetry panel, talia ops runbook. i'll draft RFC and tasks.

maya: one small but high ROI feature — export existing manual flags into a blueprint (export -> create blueprint). saves a ton of copy/paste.

aisha: huge +1. export flow should capture telemetry sampling, quotas, and failover hints.

rupert: note: ledger changes touch billing; we need a gate and a small migration that reconciles historical claimed capacity.

jon: i'll schedule a 30m sync and post the RFC link here. drop async comments if you have edge cases. thanks :thumbsup:
